scheme.authorization: AWEB-Hook DIDKey <did:key> <signature>, the signature over the canonical signed payload: exactly 86 characters of the standard base64 alphabet, no padding, zero trailing bits
scheme.body: canonical JSON {hook_event: strict unpadded base64url signing bytes, signature: the envelope signature}
scheme.certificate: a client delivery carries the member's team certificate in X-AWID-Team-Certificate, encoded as team-auth encodes it; it must be signed by the team's current key and name the event's team, producer key and certificate id; a server delivery carries none
scheme.order: audience and binding are required options; scheme; signed payload strict and canonical; signature by the header did:key; auth; payload fields; did_key equals the header's; v; team_id; aud; method and path; body_sha256; timestamp; binding_id; body; the event (with the credential's team); event_id; producer, kid and did_key equal the event's producer; for a client, the certificate
scheme.payload_fields: v, auth (hook-delivery), aud (the target's origin), method, path (raw path and query), body_sha256, team_id, binding_id, event_id, producer, kid, did_key, timestamp
scheme.producer: core, app:<app_id> or client:<certificate_id>; kid is the server producer's kid, or member for a client producer
scheme.receive_options: what the target knows independently: its own public origin, the binding the delivery must name, the team's current controller key read fresh from the registry, and its clock
scheme.signed_payload: X-AWEB-Signed-Payload carries the canonical payload, strict unpadded base64url
scheme.timestamp: UTC to the second in its one canonical spelling; refused when more than 300 seconds from the receiver's clock
scheme.what_it_proves: these checks prove self-consistency and, for a client, membership by certificate; a server producer's authority comes from resolving its registered key and active production through the team's server
